extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and others interested in submitting or learning about the National Book Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Information and high-level criteria about the National Book Awards — the categories honored, the award mission, eligibility/publication-year expectations, submission/deadline guidance, and post-award medallion/image-rights policies for winners and honorees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories honored
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards currently honor the best Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Translated Literature, and Young People’s Literature, published each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although other categories have been recognized in the past, the current categories are those five; submissions should be made into the appropriate category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication-year eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles honored are those "published each year."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied requirement that eligible works must be published within the award year; see Deadlines & Guidelines for specific date ranges and cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award mission / selection principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Book Foundation's mission is to celebrate the best of American literature, to expand its audience, and to enhance the cultural value of great writing in America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is oriented toward literary excellence and cultural contribution within the Foundation’s mission; for detailed selection criteria consult the Foundation's How the National Book Awards Work materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines & Guidelines: Eligibility, the submissions process, current prizes, guidelines, FAQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific eligibility rules, entry procedures, fees (if any), and deadlines are provided on the Deadlines & Guidelines page; prospective submitters must follow those formal rules to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medallions and image/seal rights for honored titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Seals and digital image rights are available for NBA Winner, Finalist, and Longlist titles. In addition to medallions for individual titles, medallions are also offered for 5 Under 35 honorees and Distinguished Contribution to American Letters medalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners, Finalists, and Longlisted titles (and specified honorees) may use official seals and digital images; the 5 Under 35 medallions can be used for future titles and Distinguished Contribution medallions for backlist titles — consult Medallions page for usage rules and assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical precedent and prestige
rubrics_metrics.description: Established in 1950, the National Book Awards have honored a pantheon of prominent writers (e.g., Faulkner, Morrison, Pynchon, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not an eligibility rule, the Awards' long history and list of past winners communicates expectations of high literary quality and stature for consideration.
